column1: # Tools bundled by build.sh: downloaded with eget for the target system, or
# built for a target profile by build-tools.sh.
# Columns: name repo file assets source
#   repo    GitHub owner/name, or cross:NAME to build from source with
#           cross/NAME.sh ARCH OUT (e.g. tmux with the Jetson Yocto SDK).
#   file    binary to extract from the release asset (an eget --file glob);
#   assets  "|"-separated alternatives tried in order; each alternative is a
#           means no filters. Package and checksum files are always
#           excluded. eget picks among what is left using --system, but a
#           filter that leaves one asset wins even for the wrong CPU, so
#           every download is checked with elf_arch and the next alternative
#           tried. On armv7l each alternative is first tried with an extra
#   source  how build-tools.sh makes it for a profile (see its header):
#           release (the eget columns above). Rows sharing a crates.io name
#           with another project (usbtree), needing C libraries the
#           static build lacks (rustnet: libpcap, atuin: OpenSSL, tracexec:
#           libbpf/libelf, comchan: fontconfig), not building against musl
#           (cyme), crashing rustc under fat LTO (zellij) or having go.mod
#           replace directives go install refuses (ctop) use release.
# Static musl builds come first so binaries run on older glibc (JetPack 4 is
# Ubuntu 18.04). A tool with no build for an arch is skipped with a warning.
